title: [Core][Model] torch.compile for layernorm in commandr

experiments.name: commandr_layernorm_latency
experiments.workload: CohereForAI/c4ai-command-r-v01, tp=4, benchmark_latency.py default batch-size=8 on GPU; avg decode latency per run.
experiments.note: Diff extracts commandr LayerNorm math into a standalone @torch.compile layer_norm_func so torch compiles it once instead of recompiling whenever self changes. Number source: PR body batch-size=8 avg latency 2.9004 s -> 2.7343 s (~5% latency improvement; throughput 3290.22 -> 3463.78 tok/s consistent).

reported.scope: full command-r forward-pass avg latency at tp=4 batch=8, not the isolated layernorm op the diff compiles
reported.scale_short: Author's latency is the whole command-r decode step; the diff only compiles the layernorm function. TO MAKE 1:1: microbench the isolated layer_norm_func on a command-r-shaped hidden-state tensor, base eager vs compiled.
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (s) but 2.9004 -> 2.7343 s is the whole-model avg decode latency (tp=4, batch=8), dominated by attention and MLP; the ~5% reflects the layernorm compile win diluted across the full step. Direction genuine; absolute seconds are whole-step, not the isolated layernorm op.

environment: reported-only: author's published numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
